data.title: StratusLIVE Introduces Ignite, an Active Intelligence Platform Built for Growing Nonprofits
data.description:
AI teammates work within a single constituent record. People approve every send.

CHESAPEAKE, Va., Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- StratusLIVE today introduced Ignite, the Active Intelligence Platform for cause-oriented nonprofits whose missions are growing faster than their teams. Ignite provides CRM, fundraising, finance, marketing, and engagement on a single constituent record and includes AI teammates that research, draft, and flag items that need attention. Staff review and approve; nothing sends until they do.

Most mid-size nonprofits run three to five disconnected systems. The donor records live in one, the gift posts in another, the email tool keeps its own list, and finance closes the month from a spreadsheet. The time spent carrying information between those systems is unpaid staff capacity. StratusLIVE calls it the System Tax, and it built Ignite to remove it.

"Every nonprofit leader we talk to describes the same week: more mission, same team, and hours lost moving data between tools," said Jim Funari, CEO and founder of StratusLIVE. "Ignite puts the whole relationship on one record and gives the team digital teammates that do the research and the drafting. People stay in charge of every decision. That is the only version of AI a nonprofit can put in front of its board."

One platform, one record

Ignite CRM, Ignite Fundraising, Ignite Finance, Ignite Marketing, Ignite Engagement, Ignite Partnerships, Ignite Self-Service, and Ignite Design Studio share a single constituent record, so a gift, an event registration, an email reply, and a finance posting all describe the same person. Ignite Finance carries gifts to the ledger with balanced export files for common accounting systems.

AI teammates, with people in charge

Ignite Intelligence brings AI teammates into the same platform. The roster includes Prospect Research, Major Gift, Retention, and Constituent Support teammates. They work from the organization's own data and inside its workflow, not in a separate tab. Prospect scoring uses evidence-gated bands, and every recommendation carries its sources.

Governance is built in rather than added on: read-only by default, approval gates configured by the organization, and a full audit trail. StratusLIVE maintains a current SOC 2 Type II report, available on request.

"When AI shows up in a discovery call, the first question is never 'what can it do.' It is 'who is accountable for what it does,'" said Debbie Snyder, Chief Revenue Officer at StratusLIVE. "Ignite answers that question the way a board would want it answered."

About StratusLIVE

StratusLIVE builds nonprofit software. Ignite, the Active Intelligence Platform, connects CRM, fundraising, finance, marketing, engagement, and AI teammates on one constituent record. StratusLIVE 365 serves enterprise nonprofits on Microsoft Dynamics 365. Founded in 2008 and headquartered in Chesapeake, Virginia, StratusLIVE is built by a team that comes mostly from nonprofit work.

data.title: Exxon Mobil shuts down Joliet refinery after power outage
data.description:
NEW YORK, Sept 14 (Reuters) - Exxon Mobil brought its 264,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) refinery in Joliet, Illinois, offline after a power outage occurred on Sunday, the company said on Monday.

The outage occurred at about 3:30 p.m. CT on Sunday and power was restored at around 7:00 p.m., according to a company statement. 

The outage triggered the refinery's safety flare and resulted in a shutdown.

The company said it is assessing the refinery's status, and the cause of the incident remains under investigation.

Units are being stabilized after the plant-wide shutdown, IIR Energy said in a note, adding the refinery is expected return to normal service by the end of this week.

The Joliet refinery supplies key fuels to consumers in the U.S. Midwest. It can produce about 11 million gallons a day of gasoline and diesel fuel, according to the company website.

The disruption comes amid a tight global fuel market. The Iran war and Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries have strained fuel supplies, while strong exports have further tightened domestic inventories.

The U.S. national average price of diesel last week surpassed $6 a gallon for the first time ever. Any prolonged operational disruptions could exacerbate an already tight fuel market, sending prices even higher.

(Reporting by Nicole Jao in New YorkEditing by Nick Zieminski and Will Dunham)

data.title: Wall Street drops as AI worries pummel chipmakers
data.description:
Sept 14 (Reuters) - Wall Street dipped on Monday, weighed down by losses in Nvidia ( NVDA ) and other chipmakers after top executives in U.S. artificial intelligence companies raised safety concerns and called for a slowdown in the development of AI.

Investors were also jittery after the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield briefly surpassed 5% for the first time since 2023 ahead of this week's Federal Reserve meeting. The U.S. central bank is widely expected to raise interest rates.

AI-linked stocks plunged worldwide after the leaders of Anthropic, OpenAI and xAI warned of risks from rapid development, the starkest threat yet to the billions of dollars being poured into the industry that have driven markets to record highs.

Shares of Nvidia ( NVDA ) declined 2.6%, while Broadcom ( AVGO ), Micron Technology ( MU ) and Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) each fell around 4%.

The PHLX chip index tumbled 5.4%, reducing its 2026 gain to 58%.

Brent crude futures advanced 1% to $106 as worries about energy supplies mounted following new strikes on Saudi Arabian energy infrastructure and attacks on ships in the Middle East.

High inflation, heavy corporate and government borrowing and concerns about the long-term U.S. fiscal trajectory have sent U.S. Treasury yields higher in the past month. The 5% mark that the 10-year yield hit on Monday is a threshold that analysts warned could ripple through the U.S. economy and threaten the bull market in stocks by denting the relative appeal of U.S. equities.

Traders are pricing in a 90% chance that the Fed will raise interest rates by 25 basis points at its policy meeting on Wednesday to fight inflation related to high oil prices, according to CME's FedWatch.

"The 10-year going above 5% is huge and speaks volumes, and it may pressure the Fed to do more than just one rate hike," said Jake Dollarhide, CEO of Longbow Asset Management.

The S&P 500 was down 0.27% at 7,636.02 points.

The Nasdaq declined 0.10% to 26,306.65 points, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 0.27% at 52,433.44 points.

ServiceNow ( NOW ), Adobe and Workday rallied between 4% and 8%. Those and other software stocks have sold off in recent sessions over worries that competition from AI companies could hurt their margins.

The S&P 500's recent decline, coupled with a strong earnings outlook, has the benchmark trading at 19 times expected earnings. That is its cheapest since April 2025, when U.S. President Donald Trump's "Liberation Day" tariff announcements threw global markets into a tailspin.

Eight of the 11 S&P 500 sector indexes declined, led lower by industrials, down 1.59%, followed by a 1.22% loss in utilities.

Advancing issues outnumbered falling ones within the S&P 500 by a 1.1-to-one ratio.

The S&P 500 posted nine new highs and eight new lows; the Nasdaq recorded 41 new highs and 174 new lows.

(Reporting by Niket Nishant and Tharuniyaa Lakshmi in Bengaluru; Editing by Sherry Jacob-Phillips, Pooja Desai and David Gregorio)

zPayments is now live on Base, bringing Zoth’s managed settlement desk into a platform for business payouts across supported corridors. Zoth currently processes $40M in monthly payment volume, approaching a $500M annualized run rate, with payouts settling in minutes and existing partners reducing costs by up to 80% compared with traditional rails.

DUBAI, United Arab Emirates, Sept. 14, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Zoth today scaled zPayments, its fully compliant, stablecoin-native cross-border settlement platform for businesses paying out in local currency across 171 countries. It now runs on the Base ecosystem, with USDC as its primary stablecoin. Additional chains and stablecoins will be added over time, extending coverage as the platform scales toward global reach.

At launch, zPayments already reaches the corridors most platforms treat as too hard, settling into local currency across the Middle East, including the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia and Oman, and Southeast Asia, including India, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines and Vietnam, with USD coverage to 171 countries and further reach across North America, the United Kingdom, Europe and Australia. Bank payouts are available in every market, and wallet payouts in selected few. New corridors go live in sequence, each opening only after it meets the platform's standard.

Businesses in sectors including software services, commodity trading and fund distribution are increasingly using stablecoins for cross-border payments. However, converting those funds into local currency can still involve correspondent banks, foreign exchange fees and multiple intermediaries, which can add cost and delay settlement.

Managing payouts across several markets can also create additional operational work, with businesses often relying on different providers, compliance processes and reconciliation systems for each corridor.

zPayments brings these processes into a single platform. Compliance checks are handled through the platform, businesses receive a stated rate before a payment is sent, and settlement can be tracked through one system.

Across supported corridors, payments that can cost between three and six percent and take three to five business days through traditional cross-border rails can settle through zPayments in minutes and at 80% lower cost.

"The industry solved collection years ago and left the payout leg in the last century," said Pritam Dutta, Founder and CEO of Zoth. "We did not design zPayments in a spec. We ran these payouts manually, corridor by corridor, until we understood exactly what it takes to make cross-border compliance work. That is what we built into the platform. Compliance is the hard part, and it is the part we do for you."

zPayments is not a new product. It has settled for businesses as a managed desk for over a year, processing $40M a month and more than $500M to date, and now opens to a wider cohort.

“Stablecoins give businesses a global dollar, and Base gives them the rails to move it at internet speed,” says Antonio García Martínez, Head of Growth, Base. “Zoth is taking that one step further by connecting those onchain dollars to local payment systems across the world, which is how we go from moving money onchain to actually making the global financial system work onchain.”

Everything learned by settling these payouts by hand is now built into the platform. Every payout runs through Zoth’s compliance engine, with AML, CFT and Travel Rule checks completed on the platform, alongside corridor-specific documentation such as FIRC where applicable. Transactions are executed through licensed partners in each corridor, so the operational compliance burden is carried by the platform, not pushed onto the sender.

Every payout is quoted before execution through Zoth's embedded FX infrastructure. Businesses receive one stated rate before confirming a payment, with the final landed amount visible before the transaction is sent. Settlement is instant across supported corridors, and next business day where the local rail clears on a cycle, with the cutoff stated up front. The platform also records each payout, status update and compliance file in one auditable ledger, reducing the need for teams to manage different providers, records and reconciliation systems across markets.

Getting started takes one KYB process. A business partner completes onboarding once, then runs payouts through the zPayments portal with real time status visibility at every stage. Zoth's compliance engine ensures they never chase support for a status update or manage the corridors themselves. What once required a dedicated team per corridor now runs through the platform as a single upload.

"We were paying a team across four countries through three different providers, reconciling each one by hand. Now it is a single upload, reconciled to one auditable ledger" said the CFO of a services firm using zPayments.

For businesses expanding across the Global South, payout infrastructure is becoming a strategic operating layer. Teams, vendors, contractors, distributors and counterparties need to be paid across markets where traditional rails often make pricing unclear, settlement slow and compliance difficult to manage.

zPayments is built for these corridors, bringing stated pricing, minutes-based settlement where supported, and end-to-end compliance execution into one platform.

With zPayments now live on Base, businesses can begin moving payouts across supported corridors, with existing partners already reducing costs by up to 80% compared with traditional rails.

Zoth builds regulated stablecoin infrastructure for businesses that move and settle money across borders. zPayments, its cross-border settlement platform, delivers local currency payouts at one stated rate with compliance carried on the platform. Zoth Payments Limited is registered as a Money Services Business with the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada and operates through a network of licensed partners regulated in each corridor.

data.description:
(Updates prices throughout, adds analyst comment and oil settlement)

* Investors bet heavily on Fed hike

* Semiconductor stocks fall on AI CEO warnings

* Brent settles up 1% after attacks

* US 10-year Treasury yields hit 5%

By Amanda Cooper and Chibuike Oguh

NEW YORK/LONDON, Sept 14 (Reuters) - Global stocks fell on Monday as a surge in oil prices and rising government bond yields weighed on risk appetite ahead of central bank meetings in the United States and Japan this week.

On Wall Street, technology and industrial stocks led declines across the three major indexes. Artificial intelligence-related shares also came under pressure after the leaders of OpenAI and Anthropic called for a slowdown in AI development to manage risks and protect humanity.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.23%, the S&P 500 fell 0.28% and the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.16%.

The Philadelphia chip index dropped 5%.

In Europe, the STOXX 600 was down 0.49% as gains in oil and gas stocks were offset by losses in tech, which were swept lower after the concerns expressed in a letter by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, echoed by Elon Musk, who runs xAI, and Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI.

MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe fell 0.45%.

"(Markets) are down but surprisingly resilient given the wall of worry, including rates, oil prices, Fed uncertainty and the AI build-out discussion," said Mark Hackett, chief markets strategist at Nationwide.

"The news has focused on the negative," Hackett said. "... Overall, the market is quite resilient but will likely churn sideways until we get some resolution on the Fed uncertainty and the inflation pressure conversation along with September seasonality. The breakout is unlikely until October, but with macro trends and earnings strength that is the most likely outcome."

OIL PRICE SPIKE

Brent futures were settled up 1% at $105.68 a barrel, having gained almost 9% last week. Prices for diesel, gasoline and jet fuel are all far higher than they were before the Iran war, meaning a direct hit for consumers.

Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline was temporarily shut following a drone attack, according to Saudi officials. The shutdown of the pipeline, which helps Saudi Arabia avoid the Strait of Hormuz by re-routing oil to the Red Sea, threatens up to 4% of global oil supply.

"There's been no real equity-market drama in the face of 5% yields and high oil prices. But, clearly, one thing we have to add to the mix is that if the disruption in Hormuz continues, we're going to have to add a couple of hikes by central banks, which is what the market is pricing," Lombard Odier chief economist Samy Chaar said.

BOND YIELDS RISE

Government bond yields edged higher after posting their worst weekly performance since mid-May last week.

Benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury yields touched 5% for the first time since 2023, while Germany's 10-year bond yield climbed above 3.51%, its highest level since 2009.

Traders now attach a 90% probability of the Federal Reserve raising rates on Wednesday in what could be its first hike since mid-2023. The European Central Bank raised rates last week and indicated more may follow if inflation picks up.

Markets also imply about a 76% chance that the Bank of Japan will raise its policy rate by 25 basis points to 1.25% at Friday's meeting. The BOJ is also expected to signal the possibility of further tightening as it seeks to support the yen following intervention that helped pull the currency away from a 40-year low.

"The Fed is more impatient than it was, and central banks are more impatient than they were, the ECB included. They're not just going to let time do its work. They want to get ahead of it," Chaar said.

In currency markets, the dollar rose against major peers including the euro, yen and Swiss franc. It rose 0.42% to 154.18 against the yen and was flat at 0.816 against the Swiss franc.

The euro was 0.35% lower at $1.1556.

Gold prices fell as the U.S. dollar rose. Spot gold fell 0.93% to $4,306 an ounce.

(Reporting by Chibuike Oguh in New York Editing by Ros Russell and Will Dunham)

data.title: Summit Therapeutics Shares Rise After Partner Akeso's Ivonescimab Phase 3 Lung Cancer Study in China Shows Survival Benefit
data.description:
03:09 PM EDT, 09/14/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Summit Therapeutics ( SMMT ) shares rose approximately 5% in Monday trading, a day after the company said its partner Akeso reported updated data, including overall survival, from phase III HARMONi-2 trial of investigational bispecific antibody ivonescimab, showing a 27% reduction in the risk of death compared with pembrolizumab.

The trial conducted in China evaluates ivonescimab monotherapy against pembrolizumab monotherapy in patients with locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer, whose tumors have positive PD-L1 expression, the company said.

The HARMONi-2 data will be presented at the International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer's 2026 World Conference on Lung Cancer in Seoul, Korea on Tuesday, the company added.

Ivonescimab is approved and commercially available for indications in NSCLC in China but remains investigational and has not been approved in Summit's license territories, including the US and Europe, according to a statement.

data.title: Argentina's Milei plans bill to toughen sanctions against firms operating in Falklands
data.description:
* Milei's bold move follows Trump neutrality remarks

* Bill would widen penalties to affiliates of offshore oil rigs

* Analysts warn broader penalties could unsettle investors

By Leila Miller

BUENOS AIRES, Sept 14 (Reuters) - Argentine President Javier Milei is preparing legislation this week to toughen sanctions against companies operating in the Falkland Islands, a move analysts say raises uncertainty over whether he may escalate tensions with Britain by targeting other sectors of the disputed islands' economy.

The proposed bill will build on sanctions proceedings that Argentina's government says it has opened against at least 60 companies and individuals linked to offshore oil exploration around the islands, which Argentina calls the Malvinas and claims as its own even though Britain controls them. Argentina invaded the islands in 1982 and fought a 10-week war over them before surrendering to Britain.

Congress is set to receive Milei's 2027 budget proposal by Tuesday. It is expected to boost defense spending to address a sharper focus on sovereignty issues.

This month, U.S. President Donald Trump suggested Washington could reconsider its traditionally neutral position on the Falklands dispute. Since then, Argentina has accelerated efforts to target companies involved in oil drilling activities around the islands.

Milei's proposed legislation includes tougher penalties for unauthorized operations around the islands, congressional aide Marcelo Seghini told Reuters. He said it would extend sanctions to affiliates and cover other activities affecting Argentina's natural resources.

It follows a criminal complaint filed last week against companies linked to the Sea Lion offshore project in the Falklands.

Argentina's government has not responded to Reuters requests for comment or provided a list of companies facing sanctions proceedings, though names have been reported by local media.

Analysts said they were uncertain about the scope of Milei's proposed "national sovereignty defense" bill but called his sanctions an aggressive effort to translate Argentina's sovereignty claims into legal and commercial pressure.

"It was not a project developed over time or meticulously prepared," said Marcelo Elizondo, Argentina's representative to the International Chamber of Commerce. Trump's comments, he said, "created a climate that the government sought to exploit quickly."

Companies and investors are weighing whether sanctions could ultimately affect firms with operations in Argentina, including those involved in the country's vast Vaca Muerta shale oil formation.

The government has already faced pushback over the reported sanctions. Dutch geodata specialist Fugro published a statement saying it had been incorrectly identified by local media as collaborating with the Sea Lion project, adding that its activities in the area were limited to work on a sub-sea telecommunications cable.

BROAD SANCTIONS

Experts said the measures could complicate development of the Sea Lion project by creating a chilling effect around companies working with project owners Navitas Petroleum and Rockhopper Exploration ( RCKHF ).

Both companies have said the oilfield project holds valid licenses from the Falkland Islands government and have indicated they do not expect Milei's actions to derail development.

A government document reviewed by Reuters included a range of shareholders and financial intermediaries among companies marked for possible sanctions. They included Vanguard, First Eagle, Canaccord, Aberdeen-owned Interactive Investor and Hargreaves Lansdown.

Oil majors SLB, Baker Hughes ( BKR ) and Halliburton ( HAL ) have said in recent days they would not participate in activities on the islands.

"Without major service companies, one would have to turn to mid-sized firms with less established technical capabilities-companies that might be more expensive or slower to mobilize," Juan Jose Carbajales, a former undersecretary of hydrocarbons in the former center-left government of President Alberto Fernández.

Seghini, the congressional aide, told Reuters the Milei government was considering expanding sanctions to the fishing industry in the expected legislation, potentially targeting a sector that underpins much of the Falkland Islands economy.

"The more you widen the supply chain, the more risk you run that these sanctions will be costly to you," said Federico Merke, a political scientist at the University of San Andres in Buenos Aires.

OPPOSITION PRESSURE

The sovereignty package will be a legislative test for Milei, whose libertarian coalition lacks majorities in Congress and has struggled to secure support for some economic reforms.

Center and left-wing opponents have long accused libertarian Milei of not doing enough to defend Argentina's claim on the Malvinas, and they now say he is acting for political reasons ahead of a likely 2027 reelection bid.

"He is clearly using the Malvinas for political opportunism," said Aldo Leiva, an opposition lawmaker. "If he wanted to defend the sovereignty of the Malvinas in these two years of government, he had the tools to do it."

Marcelo Garcia, a Buenos Aires analyst at the consultancy Horizon Engage, said Milei's legislation makes investors uneasy because it may help the opposition force him to escalate measures against the United Kingdom.

"There was already concern about the elections next year, what if there's a populist backlash in Argentina?" said Garcia.

Francisco Cafiero, a former secretary for international relations at the defense ministry, said the episode reflected a broader lack of strategic clarity.

"Here, we navigate amidst uncertainty and improvisation," he said.

(Reporting by Leila Miller; additional reporting by Ian Withers, Shadia Nasralla, Ross Kerber, Sheila Dang, and Simon Jessop; Editing by Lucinda Elliott and David Gregorio)

PALO ALTO, Calif., Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Open Source Vision Foundation (OSVF), the nonprofit organization that operates OpenCV, today announced plans to enhance OpenCV support for Windows on Snapdragon®. As part of this effort, OSVF is working with Qualcomm Technologies, Inc to help make it easier for developers to build, test, optimize, and deploy computer vision applications natively on Windows devices powered by Snapdragon X Series processors.

The project will focus on native OpenCV binaries for Windows on Snapdragon, automated build-and-test infrastructure to ensure quality at scale, specific software optimizes for better performance, and additional compatibility work to resolve key software dependencies within OpenCV. Together, these improvements are intended to create a more performant and reliable path from experimentation to deployment while establishing a sustainable release process for the OpenCV community targeting Windows on Snapdragon.

"OpenCV's value comes from making computer vision practical and accessible across platforms," said Dr. Satya Mallick, CEO, OpenCV. "This work is about giving Windows on Snapdragon developers a performant, dependable and familiar OpenCV experience - from installation and testing through optimization and deployment - while building the open infrastructure needed to support the platform over time."

The work is expected to progress from experimental native builds toward validated releases intended for distribution through familiar open-source channels. Improvements will proceed through OpenCV's established review and testing processes, with progress and availability shared as milestones are completed.

"Open-source frameworks are an important part of a strong developer ecosystem," said Upendra Kulkarni, VP, Product Management, Qualcomm Technologies, Inc. "By supporting the Open Source Vision Foundation to strengthen native OpenCV support for Windows on Snapdragon, we aim to help developers build and optimize computer vision applications with greater confidence."

data.title: EU is set to propose ban on social media and AI chatbots for under-15s
data.description:
* Commission President may announce some details on Wednesday

* Companies would have to pay a supervisory fee

* EU proposals would require many months of debate before they could become law

By Foo Yun Chee

BRUSSELS, Sept 14 (Reuters) - The European Union will propose a ban restricting under 15s from social media, video sharing platforms, AI chatbots and online games, in the most sweeping plan yet to protect children from online dangers, a European Commission document seen by Reuters shows.

Concerns have mounted globally about the impact on children's health and safety of major outlets, including Meta's Facebook and Instagram, TikTok, Google's YouTube and ChatGPT.

The EU proposal is part of an EU Kids Act that European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen will present on Thursday. The former may announce some details in her State of the Union address on upcoming EU policy on Wednesday.

"The Union's approach should allow minors to benefit from the huge potential of digital services, while protecting them from abuse and exploitation. It needs to limit the access of tech companies to our children, and not the other way around," the document said.

The Commission's proposal, which will also cover video gaming platforms, allows for gradual access to the various services according to age, while the obligations imposed on the companies will depend on the type of service and the age of the children.

The Commission declined to comment.

COMPANIES WOULD HAVE TO PAY A SUPERVISORY FEE

According to the document, companies will have to pay a supervisory fee to fund regulators' enforcement and supervision.

Children from 15 onwards can set up their own accounts under the proposal, while children between 13 and 14 can ask parents to open introductory accounts for social media and video-sharing platforms under parental control and with limited contacts and strict time limits.

Accounts for children between 3 and 12 will be fully controlled by parents and will only be for child-friendly services with strict safety standards, the document said. Under-3s would have no access to the services.

Details may still change ahead of the announcement.

The Commission will need to work out the draft with EU countries and the European Parliament in the coming months before it can become law.

The draft seen by Reuters sets out requirements for companies, including avoiding addictive designs and harmful feeds.

They would also have to provide tools to enable children to easily report harmful content and effective parental control tools.

Social media and video-sharing platforms will be required to verify children's age when a user opens a new account while online games platforms will have to verify children's age before they can download games.

The companies say they take precautions and many set a minimum age of at least 13 to sign up to social media platforms.

(Reporting by Foo Yun Chee; editing by Barbara Lewis)

data.title: Global AI stocks fall as industry chiefs call for slowing development
data.description:
By Johann M Cherian and Gregor Stuart Hunter

Sept 14 (Reuters) - AI-linked stocks plunged worldwide on Monday after leaders of the biggest artificial intelligence companies warned of risks from rapid development, the starkest threat yet to the billions of dollars being poured into the industry that have driven world markets to record highs.

The selloff rippled through the industry, where companies are increasingly relying on debt and circular financing to fund ambitious AI spending plans even as global borrowing costs, reflected in multi-year-high bond yields, continue to rise.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, in a lengthy essay shared on X on Saturday, called on AI companies to slow the rate at which they advance model capabilities amid mounting fears of misuse of artificial intelligence. Both Elon Musk, who runs xAI, and Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI, said they agree with Amodei.

Altman also said the company would not proceed with an IPO this year, citing safety concerns.

Wall Street's elite tech index, the Nasdaq 100, slid 1.2% to a six-week low in early trading as chip stocks, which have led the AI sugar rush, fell the most.

"If this does lead to sort of a slowdown and a rethink of AI spending, that will have ramifications for the economy and some important sectors of the stock market, because essentially, we've been running hot based on AI spending," said Steve Sosnick, chief market analyst at Interactive Brokers.

The Philadelphia chip index dropped 5.1%, with Nvidia down 3.6%, Advanced Micro Devices off 5.6% and Micron falling 6%, while Musk's SpaceX shed 1.6%.

Semiconductor equipment makers Lam Research and Applied Materials tumbled 6% each, while tech utilities Bloom Energy lost 6.8% and GE Vernova declined 7.4%.

Europe's tech sector fell 2.2%, dragged by ASML's 5.9% decline, alongside steep losses in Infineon and Siemens Energy, while in Asia, SoftBank plunged as much as 13.2% and chipmakers TSMC and SK Hynix ( SKHY ) also retreated.

"UNACCEPTABLE" RISKS

Alarm about the potential harm from AI spiked earlier this month when Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon resigned, stating that the "people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade."

A few days later, the San Francisco-based AI lab released a threat intelligence report detailing how its Claude AI models were used for activities ranging from weapons development and cyber operations to surveillance and fraud.

Over the weekend, Amodei wrote that in six to 12 months, AI agents "could be capable of taking over the entire internet potentially causing hundreds of billions of dollars in damage." Separately, OpenAI's Altman said in an interview that risks of human extinction posed by AI were "unacceptable".

And while several U.S. lawmakers have raised concern about AI's rapid progress and called for new rules, U.S. President Donald Trump said that a "sick conspiracy" against AI and data centres exists, appearing to play down concerns expressed by industry leaders.

AI-related trades have powered much of the gains in global equities since OpenAI released ChatGPT in 2022, but more recently cyberattacks by rogue AI agents and public discontent with data centre construction have raised opposition to the development of the industry.

The U.S. and Chinese governments are expected to hold AI safety talks as part of bilateral discussions taking place this month, Reuters reported. But China's state-backed Global Times blasted the Anthropic essay in an editorial, calling it a "Cold War playbook" intended to curb the country's technological development.

A growing concern for OpenAI and Anthropic is the rising competition from more affordable Chinese models such as Moonshot AI's Kimi K3, Alibaba's Qwen and DeepSeek's offerings, which could pressure the pricing of larger, more costly models.

NOT ALL BELIEVE THE WARNINGS

Some investors dismissed the warnings from Anthropic and OpenAI.

Michael Burry, whose prescient bets against the U.S. housing market before the 2008 financial crisis were chronicled in the movie "The Big Short", said in a message on X the warnings were "hype and puffery" and "cover for real uncontrollable slowing growth".

Others have argued that record capital spending commitments suggest AI development is unlikely to slow, such as Morgan Stanley's CEO, Ted Pick, who forecast earlier this year that AI spending will surpass $1.3 trillion by 2027.

"The key question is whether this is the first sign that the extraordinary AI investment cycle might eventually moderate. For now, that seems unlikely. The competitive race between companies and countries remains intense, and it's difficult to imagine firms voluntarily stepping back while rivals continue to push ahead," Deutsche Bank said in a note.

Meanwhile, Amodei's Anthropic has pushed ahead with its public debut, expected next month as sources told Reuters that the company is in talks to bring in Nvidia as an anchor investor.

Japanese chipmaker Kioxia Holdings ( KXHCF ) is also considering raising at least $10 billion by listing American depositary receipts, a report said.

(Reporting by Gregor Stuart Hunter in Singapore, Johann M Cherian, Purvi Agarwal and Utkarsh Tushar Hathi in Bengaluru; Additional reporting by Rocky Swift in Tokyo; Editing by Muralikumar Anantharaman and Saumyadeb Chakrabarty)

data.title: Artificial Agency Integrates Agentic Behavior into First Commercial Video Game in Dimensional Double Shift’s New Single Player Mode
data.description:
EDMONTON, Alberta, Sept. 14, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Artificial Agency, an AI company pioneering agentic behavior for gaming, today announced that it has integrated its Behavior Engine into Owlchemy Labs’ Dimensional Double Shift, powering an all-new Single Player Mode. The mode brings the game’s signature collaborative multiplayer experience to solo players with a full AI crew of Totally Expendable Multi-dimensional Personnel (T.E.M.P.s) robotic coworkers, each filling a distinct cooperative gameplay role. This is the world’s first commercial game mode built around moment-to-moment collaboration between one human player and multiple AI agents that interpret player intent, coordinate with one another, and adapt as the game unfolds. Artificial Agency’s technology and game-specific models provide the behavioral layer for these interactions and decisions, bringing Owlchemy Labs’ creative vision and gameplay design to life. Single Player Mode is slated to ship in the first half of 2027.

Distinct from classic “bot” implementations in previous single player game modes which respond to a pre-mapped sequence of actions, the T.E.M.P.s interact with the player in a complex, open-ended way that creates more room for player expression and individual choice. The player can speak naturally, and the T.E.M.P.s interpret requests, coordinate with the player and one another, decide how to help, and invoke approved actions within Owlchemy’s defined roles and boundaries to keep the shift moving in a busy setting like a diner. The T.E.M.P.s can also draw on relevant earlier moments, improvise within their roles, and express humor, skepticism, and other human-like personality traits authored by Owlchemy and powered by Artificial Agency’s technology.

“For years, cooperative games have relied on human teammates for communication, coordination, and role fulfillment to provide the most entertaining experience. Artificial Agency’s advances in agentic behavior have shown it’s possible to create rich experiences without compromise,” said Andrew Eiche, CEO at Owlchemy. “By integrating the Behavior Engine into Dimensional Double Shift’s new Single Player Mode, we can preserve the teamwork at the heart of game and make the experience accessible to solo players when real-life friends are not around or in off-hours of the day—all without changing the core mechanics or dynamics of multiplayer. We were able to keep our current pipeline unmodified and use agents to turn your voice into action. Everything else is traditional Owlchemy Labs. That’s a big deal for us from a development perspective and for our players.”

With this integration, Artificial Agency has made significant advancements in its training and model architecture which has unlocked commercial viability for cost-effective deployment at scale in game titles and other applications. The video game industry is bigger than ever as global revenues are expected to reach $300B by 2029, but competition to capture player attention is fierce, with more than 225,000 new games released in 2025 alone. Agentic AI presents one of the most significant emerging opportunities for studios to innovate gameplay and captivate player attention, but high recurring inference costs tied to persistent agents has served an economic challenge to game studios already under budget pressure. At the same time, developers face hurdles ensuring agents are fast and responsive in game settings.

Artificial Agency trained a small, optimized model specifically for Dimensional Double Shift, in combination with its reflex architecture to separate fast, immediate reactions from decisions that benefit from deeper model reasoning and help behavior stay responsive as gameplay changes. The result is dynamic behavior with lower latency and inference costs, making agentic gameplay commercially viable at scale and practical across a broad range of platforms including PCs, mobile, VR, and consoles.

“Three years ago, we founded Artificial Agency on a clear thesis: commercially viable agentic behavior in games requires a game-native approach,” said Brian Tanner, CEO and co-founder of Artificial Agency. “Our work with Owlchemy Labs on Dimensional Double Shift’s Single Player Mode proves it. At the heart of that approach is what we call agent empathy: designing from the agent’s point of view so it can perceive, understand, and act reliably inside the game. By closing the reality gap between what the agent believes and what is actually happening, we can train very small, game-specific models that deliver responsive, adaptive gameplay beyond what scripting can achieve, at a cost developers can ship.”

Artificial Agency’s partnership with Owlchemy Labs is a significant milestone for the company. As the first shipped game built with the Behavior Engine, Dimensional Double Shift’s Single Player Mode offers a category-defining experience, serving as powerful proof of the company’s founding vision for how agentic behavior can rethink the way games are designed and experienced.

To learn more about the Behavior Engine and partnering with Artificial Agency, click here.

Artificial Agency is an AI company pioneering agentic behavior for gaming. Its Behavior Engine trains game-specific models that enable characters and game systems to react, coordinate, and adapt to player actions and changes in game state, while reducing latency and inference costs to make agentic gameplay practical to build and ship at scale. With AI talent from Google DeepMind, gaming veterans from top AAA studios, and backing from Radical Ventures and Toyota Ventures, Artificial Agency is redefining the boundaries of gaming and completely reimagining the player experience.

data.title: Endpoint Clinical Acquires Bluefin, a Provider of Clinical Supply Forecasting and Planning Technology
data.description:
This acquisition expands Endpoint into clinical supply planning while keeping Bluefin independent and RTSM-agnostic.

RALEIGH, N.C. and BOSTON, Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Endpoint Clinical L.P., a global leader in randomization and trial supply management ("RTSM") solutions and a portfolio company of Arsenal Capital Partners, today announced it has acquired Bluefin, a Boston-based provider of clinical supply forecasting and planning technology.

The acquisition expands Endpoint into clinical supply chain planning while keeping Bluefin focused on its core forecasting and planning mission. Bluefin will operate independently and continue to connect with RTSM systems across the industry. Endpoint will support Bluefin with global project management, implementation, quality, and customer support capabilities to help sponsors deploy the platform reliably and efficiently.

"Clinical supply planning is becoming more complex, more connected to trial execution, and more dependent on timely intelligence," said Nagaraja "Sri" Srivatsan, Chief Executive Officer of Endpoint Clinical. "Bluefin gives Endpoint a strong foundation in clinical supply planning while preserving customer choice across RTSM providers. Together, we have the opportunity to bring intelligence into every aspect of clinical supply, connecting planning, forecasting, enrollment signals, inventory movement, and RTSM execution data so every sponsor can make faster, better-informed decisions across all their studies. Endpoint can also bring the implementation discipline and support needed to deploy these capabilities reliably at scale."

Clinical supply teams have long recognized that better outcomes come from connecting supply plans to the data that trials generate in real time; the challenge has been bringing those data sources together in a way that supports timely, actionable decision-making. Endpoint and Bluefin are helping close that gap, linking supply plans to trial execution data so teams can anticipate enrollment shifts and automate forecasting rather than react to them. Bluefin will maintain its open, RTSM- and forecasting-agnostic model, which both companies see as core to advancing the industry.

"We're thrilled to be joining the Endpoint team," said Andy Maltun, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Bluefin. "The connection between RTSM and clinical supply forecasting is so natural that it's one of the first opportunities we discuss with every sponsor. Together, we are building a clinical supply intelligence platform that uses modern technology to automate manual work, reduce risk, and lower cost through optimized supply plans."

"This acquisition is consistent with our strategy of building technology-rich companies that solve meaningful enterprise problems for healthcare customers," said Mark A. Goldberg, MD, Chairman of the Board of Directors of Endpoint Clinical and Operating Partner at Arsenal Capital Partners. "Endpoint gains a path into clinical supply planning, Bluefin gains resources to scale, and the market continues to benefit from an independent planning platform that works across any RTSM environment." Arsenal acquired Endpoint Clinical in 2024 and continues to support the company's growth and evolution of its RTSM platforms and AI capabilities.

By bringing clinical supply planning closer to real-time trial execution, Endpoint and Bluefin aim to give sponsors greater intelligence and confidence in managing increasingly complex global studies.

For more information, visit Endpoint Clinical and Bluefin.

About Endpoint Clinical

Endpoint Clinical is a trusted clinical trial technology and service partner that delivers reliable RTSM solutions. Endpoint blends seamlessly into clinical trial processes by providing anticipatory and adaptive solutions to proactively mitigate risks. With decades of experience, Endpoint offers a deep understanding of the challenges that sponsors and CROs face. Its tech-forward dedication to innovation and high-touch services enable Endpoint to control the controllables and proactively generate speedy, strategic solutions, so sponsors and CROs can focus on running seamless clinical trials.

Bluefin is a clinical supply forecasting and planning technology company focused on helping sponsors and CROs make smarter, data-driven supply decisions. Its platform enables organizations to forecast demand, evaluate supply scenarios, optimize distribution strategies, and proactively manage supply risk across the clinical trial lifecycle. Through advanced modeling and planning capabilities, Bluefin helps clinical supply teams improve visibility, increase operational confidence, and support more efficient trial execution.

Since its inception in 2000, Arsenal has raised institutional equity investment funds totaling more than $10 billion, completed more than 300 platform and add-on acquisitions, and achieved more than 35 realizations. data.title: Soccer-Manchester derby VAR stood down from Premier League duty
data.description:
Sept 14 (Reuters) - Matt Donohue, the video assistant referee (VAR) who allowed Erling Haaland's winner in Manchester City's 1-0 victory over Manchester United ( MANU ), has not been selected to officiate at any of next weekend's Premier League fixtures.

Assistant VAR Blake Antrobus has also not been given any assignment after refereeing body Pro Ref acknowledged in a statement that VAR was wrong to allow Haaland's decisive goal.

The decision was taken by chief refereeing officer Howard Webb and the management team, with neither official expected to return to duty until at least after the international break.

Haaland's second-half strike was initially ruled out for offside before being awarded following a VAR review that determined the Norwegian striker was onside.

However, the refereeing body later said the VAR had failed to take into account the impact of teammate Enzo Fernandez, who attempted to play the ball from an offside position.

(Reporting by Paras J. Haji in Bengaluru, editing by Pritha Sarkar)

data.title: VIP Announces Strategic Acquisition of Encompass Technologies to Accelerate the Future of Food & Beverage Technology
data.description:
Acquisition expands access to technology and accelerates AI innovation across the food & beverage industry

COLCHESTER, Vt., Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- VIP, a leading technology partner to the food and beverage industry, today announced the completion of its acquisition of Encompass Technologies, further strengthening VIP's commitment to delivering innovative technology across the food and beverage ecosystem.

The acquisition expands VIP's portfolio of technology capabilities and creates new opportunities for customers of both companies. By bringing together Encompass' technology and talent with VIP's scale, industry expertise, customer relationships, and continued investment in innovation, the combined companies can deliver more value to customers and accelerate the pace of modernization. Together, the companies will be better positioned to serve suppliers, distributors, and retailers throughout the ecosystem. The companies will continue to operate under their respective names and brands.

The acquisition is another step in VIP's long-term strategy to broaden access to technology, accelerate innovation, and invest in the capabilities that will define the next generation of food and beverage technology.

"This is an incredibly exciting moment for VIP, our customers, and the broader food and beverage industry," said Andrew Criezis, CEO of VIP. "The industry is at an important inflection point. Technology is moving faster than ever, and AI is creating new possibilities for how businesses operate, make decisions, and serve their customers. Together, VIP and Encompass bring important capabilities and expertise that will allow us to expand what we offer our customers and accelerate the pace of innovation for the industry." Criezis will remain CEO across the respective companies.

Accelerating AI and Intelligent Technology

VIP has continued to invest in modern technology, connected solutions, and agentic workflows designed to help food and beverage companies navigate increasing complexity and operate with greater intelligence and agility. The addition of Encompass expands that foundation, bringing new capabilities and expertise that can help customers anticipate what's next, automate increasingly complex work, optimize operations in real time, and turn data into actionable insight.

VIP believes the next generation of food and beverage technology will move beyond traditional software toward intelligent systems that can increasingly understand context, interpret data, recommend actions, and help execute work.

"AI will be a key part of this evolution. The food and beverage industry has an incredible opportunity to harness technology and AI to operate differently, and we want to help accelerate that transformation," said Criezis. "Encompass expands our capabilities and strengthens our ability to invest, innovate and move faster. Together, we can give this industry and our customers greater access to technology that helps them solve more of their most important challenges and create better outcomes for their businesses."

More Technology. Greater Access. Faster Innovation.

For customers of both VIP and Encompass, the acquisition creates access to a broader range of technology capabilities, expertise, and innovation. By bringing together complementary strengths, customers of both companies will benefit from continued investment in product development, data, AI, and integration, as well as new opportunities to connect complementary capabilities across the broader VIP platform. For VIP customers, the acquisition expands the range of solutions available to address their evolving needs from a trusted technology partner. For Encompass customers, it brings the scale, resources, and industry expertise of VIP behind the continued evolution of the products and solutions they rely on today. Continued investment across both organizations will unlock new capabilities and create opportunities for an even more connected customer experience.

"We've always believed the food and beverage industry deserves technology that helps businesses move faster, operate smarter, and better serve their customers," said Patrick Tickle, CEO of Encompass Technologies. "Joining VIP gives Encompass an incredible opportunity to build on what we've created and accelerate that vision. By bringing together Encompass' technology and talent with VIP's scale, industry expertise, customer relationships, and continued investment in innovation, we believe we can deliver more value to our customers and help shape the next generation of technology for this industry. We're incredibly proud of what the Encompass team has built and excited about what we can accomplish together."

Tickle will remain CEO of Encompass through the transition before moving into an advisor role.

Investing in the Future of Food and Beverage Technology

The food and beverage industry is entering a period of significant transformation. Increasing operational complexity, evolving customer expectations, and rapid advances in AI are creating both new challenges and opportunities across the industry.

VIP believes businesses that embrace this transformation will have the opportunity to operate fundamentally differently, with greater automation, better visibility, faster decision-making, and technology that increasingly works alongside their teams.

The acquisition of Encompass Technologies represents another step in VIP's strategy to expand its capabilities, accelerate innovation, and help the food and beverage industry move faster into its next era of intelligent technology.

VIP is a leading technology partner to the food and beverage industry, providing software, data, analytics, automation, and business solutions that help companies operate more efficiently and make smarter decisions. For decades, VIP has combined deep industry expertise with technology innovation to help its customers grow and succeed. Today, VIP is investing in the next generation of its platform, including AI-powered solutions designed to transform how work gets done across the food and beverage ecosystem.

Its platform brings together capabilities across ERP, operations, sales, logistics, and data to help customers improve efficiency, visibility, and decision-making.

data.title: Fed Set to Raise Rates This Week, Signal Another Hike Later in 2026, UBS Says
data.description:
01:08 PM EDT, 09/14/2026 (MT Newswires) -- The Federal Reserve is expected to raise interest rates by 25 basis points at this week's policy meeting, with its latest "dot plot" likely signaling another hike later this year, UBS Securities said in a note e-mailed Monday.

The Federal Open Market Committee kicks off its two-day meeting on Tuesday, with a decision due Wednesday. The committee will also publish its Summary of Economic Projections document that includes FOMC members' anonymous expectations regarding monetary policy, dubbed the dot plot.

The Bureau of Labor Statistics' consumer and producer price reports last week failed to improve the inflation outlook, UBS said. Consumer inflation and producer prices hit three-month highs in August as energy costs rose, official data showed.

Markets are currently pricing in a 90% probability that the Fed will raise the benchmark lending rate by 25 basis points this week, according to the CME FedWatch tool. The remaining odds point to another central bank pause.

A hike on Wednesday would mark a major shift in policy following five consecutive FOMC decisions to keep rates steady. UBS economists including Jonathan Pingle are projecting a 10-2 vote in favor of policy tightening, with governors Christopher Waller and Michelle Bowman likely to vote for a hold.

"We expect the assumptions of appropriate policy to be split on the issue of whether one or two 0.25 (percentage point) rate hikes would be appropriate this year, but risks tilt toward two," Pingle wrote. "In the press conference, we do not expect Chairman (Kevin) Warsh to provide much future signal on the path of policy ahead, but if the FOMC actually raises rates that act alone should further empower his tough sounding hawkish rhetoric."

In his late-August Jackson Hole speech, Warsh said that the central bank's primary focus should be on prices, given that the US is doing well on the employment front. Earlier this month, Waller said he would support keeping interest rates steady if further signs of disinflation emerge, though he also seemed willing to tighten monetary policy if price pressures intensify.

Eighteen FOMC members will likely submit policy dots, with Warsh again not expected to submit his projections, according to UBS.

"We would not be surprised to see 10 participants assume two or more (25-basis-point) rate hikes would be appropriate this year," Pingle said. "Participants would be revising up their dots as they revise down their inflation projections, which is very rare, and we expect the FOMC members themselves remain somewhat divided on whether rate hiking needs to resume at this time."

The need for more rate hikes will likely dissipate into 2027 as the base effects of the energy price shock lap, Pingle said.
